TastingNotes: Now at eight years of age, the 2017 Aile d'Argent Blanc from Château Mouton Rothschild is shining beautifully. It greets you with a radiant straw-yellow color and an inviting bouquet of exotic fruits, where ripe lychee, guava and even a hint of banana mingle with notes of white peach and citrus. On the palate, those vibrant flavors carry through in a medium to full-bodied wine with a smooth, almost creamy texture, balanced by lively acidity that gives it energy and lift. The finish is long and refined, with a streak of stony minerality and a pleasant hint of bitterness that adds complexity. It leaves you with a lasting impression of tropical fruit and elegance.

Medium-bodied for Pomerol, with a long, savory finish that's drinking beautifully today.

Wine: Domaine de la Janasse Châteauneuf-du-Pape Cuvée Chaupin
TastingNotes: Very concentrated flavors with a lot of complexity and depth. A little hot (15.5% ABV), which I'm guessing is a result of the high concentration and thus initial sugar content that needed to be fermented away. To an extent though, the higher alcohol content was needed to go toe-to-toe with the extracted flavors. Drank the 2020 in 2023 and it was too young. Would love to revisit in another 5 years.
